bug_semantics: A Tor onion-service client accepted a RENDEZVOUS_ESTABLISHED cell from the rendezvous point based only on circuit purpose CIRCUIT_PURPOSE_C_ESTABLISH_REND, without recording whether it had actually sent ESTABLISH_RENDEZVOUS. hs_ident is allocated with tor_malloc_zero, and both the 20-byte rendezvous cookie and the client ntor keypair are filled only inside hs_circ_send_establish_rendezvous (which also regenerates them on every call). If that send is skipped, raced, or has not yet happened—client_rendezvous_circ_has_opened can return early when node_supports_v3_rendezvous_point fails, and circuit_get_open_circ_or_launch can call circuit_has_opened on an already-open cannibalized rend circuit—the RP can inject an unsolicited RENDEZVOUS_ESTABLISHED. The client then marks the circuit C_REND_READY and may emit INTRODUCE1 with a still-zero cookie/keypair, after which the RP can complete RENDEZVOUS2 as if it were the onion service (CWE-362).
flaw_origin: The v3 client first grew this sink in the 2017 prop224 series. b91693f7c3099c691d0e5dbb60ac55df14b7bd68 added hs_circ_send_establish_rendezvous (cookie+keypair generated on every send, no sent-flag) and wired it from client_rendezvous_circ_has_opened. The immediate child 89eb96c19a091b1e892e4a7c05f06e188131aed0 first wrote hs_client_receive_rendezvous_acked, which promoted the circuit to C_REND_READY after a purpose-only check and replaced the v2 dispatch. Those receive-handler lines then survived unchanged until the 2026 fix; git log -L shows no intermediate rewrite. The project's 'bugfix on 0.3.5.3-alpha' is later than this first write (first tag tor-0.3.2.1-alpha); 0.3.5 was a src/or -> src/feature/hs modularization window, not a new first-write.
